card.name: Punctuation inside lists of health risk factors
card.fires_on: Commas, colons, 'and' or 'to' that sit inside or just before a list of public-health risk factors, such as tobacco, diet, inactivity, alcohol and speeding. The pole fires on the joining mark, not on the risk words.

modes.label: Comma between risk factors
modes.description: A comma after one item in a list of causes or risk factors, before the next item.
modes.example: 43% of cancer deaths worldwide are due to tobacco, unhealthy diet<<,>> physical inactivity and infections (3).

modes.label: Linking word before a risk
modes.description: 'and' or 'to' that joins or introduces risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol.
modes.example: Tobacco use<< and>> excessive alcohol consumption have been estimated to account

modes.label: Colon or numbered list
modes.description: A colon or closing bracket that introduces or continues an enumerated list of risk behaviors.
modes.example: providing guidance to countries on five key risk factors<<:>> speeding, drinking and driving, and failing

card.writes: The promoted tokens (swim, swimming) are unrelated to the context, so there is no clear output effect.
card.plain: It marks the commas and linking words in a list of lifestyle or environmental health risks like tobacco, diet and alcohol.
